title: Exclusive Interview Mason Graham
text: Coming to you live today from the first voluntary mini camp practice of the Todd Monken era here with Mason Graham. Mason, first of all, good to see you, man. Welcome back. How's the off season treating you? It was good. Just, you know, time away from the facility, but, you know, it's good getting back in here, seeing some new faces, um and just, you know, starting the new year. For you, this is kind of your third year in a row with a different staff. You go back to your last year at Michigan, first year last year. What's this one been like for you so far getting to know Coach Ruttenburg and obviously familiarity with Jack Cichy there in your room? Yeah, I mean, it's not too different for me, you know, I got the same position coach. And then, Coach Ruttenburg, you know, he's kind of the same mindset, you know, he wants to still attack and penetrate up front. So, not much different for me, but um cool seeing, you know, Coach Monken come in and kind of, you know, set a new standard here. Yeah, lots of team periods today. I think that's going to be kind of a hallmark. We're going to get after play a lot of football. What was it like being out there and actually playing a little bit of football without pads, obviously, but just out there getting in the mix? Yeah, it was funny, you know, last time we played some ball with some of those guys was January. So, you know, good getting out here, you know, got some new faces, um you know, just getting comfortable with the guys again. What was the biggest thing you learned in your rookie year? Uh no, just like I don't really know, honestly. Uh if I had to say, you know, take it takes a lot to, you know, win. You know, it's hard to win in NFL. So, you know, just kind of seeing how my first year went and, you know, just how I want things to change from what year one to year two. What was something that you liked about year one and what was something that you went and took this off season time down in Dallas to to work on to to come back and improve here in year two? Yeah, kind of just reflecting on my season, you know, I feel like I had a decent season, but obviously not what I wanted, you know, um but just getting stronger was my main focus. Um just being more stout and um you know, playing against against a lot bigger guys and more experienced guys. So, uh just strength was a big thing for me. So, what did you do to work on that down in Dallas? Cuz I imagine you're stronger than just about anybody else that you're going to encounter on planet Earth. So, what's like that kind of a program that you went through this off season? Cuz you look you look great. >> Yeah, I appreciate it. But, uh just more lifting stuff, but still keeping my speed and agility. You know, that's something I'm really good at is, you know, my quickness and athleticism. So, I already knew I kind of had that, but just wanted to work on more of my strength stuff that I needed to focus on. What would you say it's been like with Todd Monken so far? Cuz he's putting his stamp on this football team, not just from practice, I mean, just even the meeting rooms. What's kind of How would you describe kind of what his his mission or his mindset that he wants you guys to have is? Uh I would just say urgent, you know, he wants to change this, you know, place around, you know. It's been like this for too long, you know, we're trying to change this around, you know. I've only been here for one year and I'm already I'm already tired of losing. So, trying to just turn this around. Is that one of the harder things that that people for people to even comprehend from a psychological standpoint is obviously Michigan, you're national champion. Guys losing two games in a year is like, "Oh my goodness." Right? The NFL, as you said, it's hard to win. Everybody is very good in the NFL. The margin is very small. Is that kind of one of the interesting things to get your head around? Yeah, I mean, it's just the little things that can separate you from winning or losing a game, you know. Feel like guys in college, you can if you're a way better team, you can make more mistakes, get away with stuff, but, you know, everyone's at the top of their game. They're out there for a reason. So, you got to be on top of your stuff. And how excited are you for this season and just getting back to work, getting after it? Really excited. Um just ready to win, you know, Coach Monken keeps on reiterating it, you know, just want to win. We all want to win and just be a part of something special. So, Absolutely. Well, Mason, good to see you again. Welcome back and let's go after it. We're just day one here. We're just laying a little foundation, long way to go, but great to see you out there on the grass today. Appreciate it.

What are the things that make you or make an NFL team remove a player from a board or want to avoid a player from a risk perspective? >> Oh man, that it can be a lot of things really. It can be have to do with, you know, practice habits or character. It can happen, you know, injury, uh, uh, history. I mean, there's just so many things and maybe just the fit of the player. You know, there may be a player that doesn't fit in our particular scheme and as good as we think he is, he just doesn't fit for what we're trying to get accomplished. So, it can be a lot of things. Uh it's not it's never just one thing. Last one. >> Um, is that dynamic kickoff rule? Is that add like a a different element to like especially day three for guys who maybe are like a one skill set type of player in like like would you be able to get like a heat or whatever and in >> as a priority free agent versus you know now? >> Yeah, I I think that's more dependent upon what your roster looks like. But look, we have to, you know, we pay attention to special teams and and uh and the kickoff rule changes have affected a little bit the makeup of of your your roster in that regard. And so there there's I wouldn't say it's a big deal, but it is, you know, it is a um it is variable.

title: Everything It Takes to Prepare for the NFL Combine | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: A lot of the work I do is behind the scenes, but it makes it worth it because I love football and I love contributing to what we're building here. >> [music] >> I'm Peyton Roth, I'm a scouting coordinator for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. [music] >> Before we head off to the combine in Indianapolis, there's a handful of items I have to check off my list here in Tampa. Mostly combine books, credentials, scheduling, making sure everyone's good to go with travel. After that, I'll work with Spencer Dill, our director of IT, to kind of build out the book. So, that kind of includes, you know, just general combine information, our informal [music] interviews, and then just our formal interviews as well. So, that will all go into the book. No two books are alike, that's very important. Once those books are completed, I'll [music] kind of get eyes on them, go through them, make sure everyone's books are good to go. Once I do that, I'll ship them out to Indy and they will be here when when I arrive. We have about 450 [music] guys that we make cut-ups for throughout the year, and these are mostly done for Jason, [music] Todd Bowles, any coach that wants to watch. These film cut-ups that we make throughout the season, they look a little [music] bit different for every position. We take evaluative plays, so good, [music] bad, big plays, and we just kind of compile it together to make a cut-up um that's easier to kind of narrow in on the player that we're talking about. So, we have a certain number [music] of color tags, so my settings are red [music] for run, blue for pass. I have three for uh PBU. >> I have four for pressure. I have five for like interception. Once I'm done watching four games, I kind of [music] sort them. I do um plays versus the run, plays versus the pass, um any big plays I want to add at the end. Once we get these All-Star [music] games in and the combine stuff and pro days, I'll put that on the back end and pretty much wraps up the cut-up. So, I land in Indy, the scouting staff uh we get here on Monday, and informal interviews [music] and formal interviews start on Monday. One of the scouting assistants will usually go grab the books from FedEx that we shipped out. Shannon Cogan always helps me out, one of our pro scouts. We'll walk over, pick up the credentials in bulk, cross-check that [music] with our rooming list, make sure everyone's credentials are good to go. Take them back to my room, I'll post up with the books and the credentials. I'll send everyone a group chat like, "Hey, swing by [music] my room, grab your stuff, and let's get going." The formal interview process is kind of crazy. And it's 20-minute [music] time slots starting at 7:00 p.m. and going all the way to 11:00 p.m. and we're usually packed during that. We have about 12 interviews. [music] So, what I'll do is, let's say the Saints are interviewing the guy that we're going to we're going to interview next, I will walk down to the Saints interview [music] suite about 5 minutes before, and then once the interview is over, I'll grab him, walk him back to our suite, >> and then the interview will restart. All 32 teams have a suite in one hallway. It's very hectic, [music] there are a lot of people. So, I think it's important that I'm there to grab the guy. [music] We have a 2-minute passing period to get to our suite, and I think that [music] if I wasn't there, you know, they may get sidetracked, you know, people might pull them aside, try to [music] talk to them, they might see their friends. So, it's important that I grab them, we kind of make small talk along the way, get to know the [music] guy, drop them off at our suite, and then I do it again. As I'm walking with them during this like 2-minute [music] passing period, I really try to just like kind of loosen the guys up. Some of them are pretty nervous, some of them it's their >> 20th interview of the week and they're fine. But, obviously we want to talk to these guys, we want to get to know these guys, will they fit in our building, will they raise the temperature of our room. Obviously, our scouts do a great job out on the road all year, but it's important for Jason, Mike, and [music] Rob to talk to these guys in person, and then obviously seeing them work out in person is huge as well. Once the workouts start, [music] I'm going to be over at 40s with Andy Spire and Tony Hardy timing all of those. It's an awesome process, it's really fun. Uh we have some friendly competition going over there, so it's a really good time. We'll time the 40s for all the positions, come back over to the suite, eat some food, [music] watch the on-field drills, then we'll do it all over again for for every position. After the draft [music] ends in April, we start on the next year. We're building out our draft board year-round. [music] We start on these guys early. So, to be at the combine in Indy, kind of seeing the picture come together, knowing the draft is, you know, a [music] month or two away, it's really cool to see all the work that we've been doing on these guys >> is paying off, and we're targeting the right guys that we think would would fit in.

title: HC Dan Quinn Sits Down with Logan Paulsen to Talk 2026 NFL Draft | Command Center | Commanders
text: Coach, always great to see you. Thanks for letting us be in your office, man. >> Yeah, it's awesome, man. Good to have you here. Too many times in the head coach's office. You're like, I don't know. >> Yeah, who know? Yeah, I was going to say, man, getting cut is a tough deal up in here. Uh, so what I'd say, coach, is this has been a crazy off seasonason for you. Two new coordinators, a huge all in free agency. Obviously, draft's coming up. Where do you think the team is at right now heading into the draft? >> Well, you know, change, that's each year that's going to be the one. And so this year a lot, you know, obviously with the free agency coaching side and now >> one more piece to come, you know, with the draft coming, but here on April 20th, this is our first time of getting everybody together. And what we'll need to see in this time is how does the team, that chemistry, that development, all of them together. But man, we're really pumped. Um, we really like where we're at and uh we're excited to get rolling. >> I'm sure, man, it's always exciting with the new season. One thing I'm pretty sure you're excited about, too, is kind of you got two new coordinators. Yep. got to kind of learn what they're about, what the system is. How fun was that process for you kind of saying, "Oh, this is how this defense works. This is how this defensive end plays." What was that process like for you? >> Yeah, that was awesome. And uh it's one of the um parts about the profession that I love the most is how do you grow, what's different, what changes, and knowing that you can be in front of some of those changes. And talking about like Dante specifically, I thought systemwise coming from Minnesota, what they've been doing, I thought Logan, they were really in front of some of the things in terms of the checks, the adjustments they were making at the line of scrimmage. I had liked what I had seen from that group and then getting to know him, the teaching background that he has, uh, it just really all came together for us. >> Yeah. And I think the other cool thing is like obviously you work with Adam quite a bit. Like how do those conversations with those guys like affect the personnel side with free agency with the draft coming up? Like how does that affect your process with the people in the building? >> Right. When we got everybody on board, um, David and Dante, staff-wise, the first thing we did was have them present to the scouts, >> to the pro scouts, the college scouts, this is the system. These are some of the traits. This is what we'd be looking for to see, is there anything changing at a position? Is there anything different that we would need to look for? Um, and so those were the things that we did right away. And so making sure from the scouting side that we're all, you know, speaking from the same >> the same book. you know, so to speak, uh, was really important. I thought like Adam and the staff and the coaches have just spent as much time as we could through free agency and now through the draft, so we're all like seeing it exactly the same. >> Yeah. And I think that's interesting you bring up like the relationship there because you bring in all these, you know, big- time pass rushers, big time, big time. And how does the free agency period affect what you're doing with the draft and your philosophy heading in? Like I think that's always a fun kind of conversation to have. >> It is. And anytime you can go and really feel comfortable to go play before the draft, you know, you're really sitting in a strong spot. And that's how we feel today because you're not we have to get this or we have to get that, we have to get this. And so going into it, it allows you um to add to the group and that's such a cool piece to it. But yeah, we're really excited about the people that we added, different pieces, some rushers, add a backer who's got inside blitz technique, some corners, obviously a tight end, and you know, just different spots, running back, you know, just different pieces to how we'd go about it. And uh >> we're able to resign some players, too, which was a big deal for us. So, yeah, we're excited with this group that we have and then to add to it here in a couple weeks. U we're pumped for that, too. >> Yeah. You talk about bringing new people in and you're always talking about your growth mindset and how you kind of always want to evolve and change and be the best version of yourself. How has that impacted the way you evaluate these guys coming out? It's like such a different game, such a different process for you. Can you talk about some of that for us? I >> think you want to find out like from a player standpoint, what are the unique things that player can bring to the team >> and can they find spaces to do that over and over again? And so like for instance in your spot for the >> people like all right this guy could run block better than most everybody but that was that was your superpower. And so Mike and the staff here they they came to find that out and recognize that and then put you in the spots to allow you to do your thing. Man I can get my helmet wide and get run. I can knock people out. >> And so that type of skill >> is really appreciated. And so as we're going through the draft process, what would the player do if they were here on our team? >> Who would they compete with? What would that look like? How would we feature them, whether it's offense or defense? And Larry Iso is a big part of the evaluations, too. He goes through a lot of their tape during college special teams or just offensively and defensively, and how would they fit into that role as well. And so when we put all those together, that's why we love the dialogue, you know, in terms of getting ready for the draft. >> Yeah. One of my favorite things about playing for you, coach, honestly, was your constant hunger for like this superpower. And so, one of the things I think people miss with the draft process in general, it's not about always the guy, but about it's about the role and situation and development. How do you ensure that you get the best the best version of these guys once they're here in the building? >> Yeah, it's interesting that you bring that up because right now, due to maybe I don't know if this is the last COVID year of class, there's players that have five and six years of experience. Some dudes are 26 years old. >> And there's others that are in that traditional three years and out. And so there's this big, you know, levels of experience to somebody who has lots of experience may have started, >> you know, over 50 55 games and then others that may have had, you know, a year and a half of starting being that they were the only at college for three years. But getting back to your initial question is where do you think that person can go to? where do you think their traits can lead them to? And maybe in year one, they may have this role, but by year two, we'd expect them to get to this spot. So, you have to have some vision of what they can be. But, um, it is interesting when you see the different levels of experience because if somebody's already 24, close to 25 coming in the NFL, they're close to maybe where their ceiling is, where others who may have only, you know, 21 and just getting rolling, like that's a big space. And uh sometimes there's a bigger gap that they can make up. >> Is there anything to to your thought process with that where it's like as a coach, can I get this guy there? Like and that's why we want him here because we think he can actualize this potential. >> Yes. And that's to me then for me to push to the coach say, okay, what's the action you'll take to help him get there? Yeah. >> Because if you think they can all right, what would that look like? And that's why you the meetings with the players can be so critical. You want to find out what type of adversity have they overcome, you know, in playing football because like we know that's going to happen 100% how hard it's going to be and how do they overcome that and what was the hardest thing to learn and skill for them. >> And so if they can articulate that and say that then we know, okay, this is a person that's already been through some things and they know how to get better. And if we can do that and have a specific plan for them, man, does it make the runway easier for them when they get here. Hey, this is what we think you can be. And oftentimes a player may not even understand that about themselves. Sure. >> It's why so oftentimes we see somebody, okay, how do you get drafted late or undrafted and just take off? >> This is the exact thing that we need you to do and that can you do it at a really high level, plan it, map it out for him, and then see if we can take him there. >> Coach, I could talk about this with you all day, but I think the thing that people want to know at home is like draft spread. We got some adversity happening in the building. >> Chef Connor's moving on. Chef Brandon's taken over. Yes. >> What's the expect? I mean, it's a big night, man. Conor used to do lobster tales and flaming, all kinds of stuff. What's Brandon's deal? And what's >> I think Brandon's really going to be dialed in. You need something to sustain us, you know, because after that pick, it's going to goes on for a long time. So, I think pizza is definitely going to be a big part of that. >> Okay. >> Um, >> chicken wings, anything like that? >> There should be that for sure. U, we've got excellent ice cream sandwiches for late Saturday. You do? You do? Yes. And so those are just a few of the staples uh that you want to make sure you have. >> It's about the proper nutrition. Yes. It's it's a marathon, not a sprint, right? >> That's right. And you want to make sure you have just the right amounts of of things as you're heading Newton through the weekend, but come Thursday, I have full confidence. Brandon is going to be ready. He's been practicing a lot, you know, this off season. So, uh I've got full confidence in him, dude. >> Coach, good luck. Thanks so much, man. Appreciate it. Thanks, Luke.

title: GM Adam Peters Previews the 2026 NFL Draft with Bryan Colbert Jr. | Command Center | Commanders
text: here in the team auditorium with the man AP Adam Peters in the building. Sir, thank you so much for taking the time. >> Thank you. >> What an off seasonason it has been for you. >> Yeah, >> it's going. You have everybody buzzing right now because of these new jerseys, showing love to the past, but also being excited about the future. How excited are you for the reaction to the new jerseys? >> Yeah, first of all, I wish I could take credit, you know, but that was the the vision of our ownership group. um and Josh and then uh our our business side making it come to life, you know, Mark Klaus and Patrick Arthur and everybody and just like everybody, social media team, marketing, just like showing like how cool uh you know, dipping into our past is and and I'm pretty juiced about it, dude. I I can't lie. Um I was really pumped when we had him last year for the throwbacks and then having those be our permanent uh uniforms just feels right. Well, something you can't take a little bit of credit for at least is this free agency pool that we just had. I mean, Dan Orlovski spoke to me a few weeks ago and said he feels the Commanders won free agency, and I know that has to be something that you really really are excited about. How do you feel about all of these new guys that we brought in? >> Um, I want I want to win the games, not free agency, right? But um but that being said, uh really excited about the guys, not not just the players, but the people that we brought in, the guys that we brought back from our own team. Uh that was really important. And then going out and getting some guys, some speed, some youth and and some real energy in the building. And it was really fun when they all came in, we signed them and and got to welcome them and you could just feel the the energy back in the building. It was it was really cool. So, um, they're coming in on Monday, uh, for, uh, the offseason program, and I can't wait. >> I appreciate the humility, man, but it's been dope watching you cook in free agency these last years. It's funny, we were talking before we started recording, and this has been a tradition for us. This is our third year sitting here before the draft. And I don't know if you remember, but last year when we sat here, I asked you about free agency, and you said if we had to play a game today, this was before the draft, you said we would be ready to play the draft. It's just a bonus. Do you feel that way about this free point where the ste team stands today? >> Yeah, I do. I think we all do. And um that's the goal. I think you never want to have glaring holes where you feel like you got to go reach for somebody um and not picking the best player available that can help your team. So, uh we feel we put ourselves in that position and and that's our mindset going into the draft. >> And you talk about the draft and there's a lot of talent in this draft all through it. But when you look at just the pool as a whole, this talent that's in the draft this year, what does it make you feel like is one of the best prospect evaluators in the game? >> Um, you know, I I think I'd start with, you know, where we're sitting at pick seven. And I feel really good about, you know, getting a really good player there. So, I think that's that's the the first first part of it. And there's so many good players at so many different spots. You know, you could really fill in the whole team and see there's going to be a good player at any position, which is cool. So we can just go ahead and pick who we think is best. But you can always find the gyms late in the draft and and that's where our our college scouts, you know, they make their hey on day three. And they've done a great job these last couple years of really um setting the table and really letting us know who they really like. You know, not just, you know, on the tape, but what what makes these guys tick, you know, the type of people they are, the the human beings, how much they love football, teammate, and all the different things that make you a great pro. So that process, although you get more attention on the first round pick, that that part's my favorite. >> Oh man, I could tell how much you love the scouting process and you guys made a little bit of headlines when you said, "Hey, we're going to go all hands on deck to Ohio State Pro Day. We know how many prospects are over there at Ohio State." What made you decide to say, "Hey, we all need to be present for this one." >> Yeah. Well, we were sitting in the draft room for about a week and it's starting to get dingy and dark, so we need to get out. I know. Um it was uh it just made sense. Honestly, it made sense where um we it's it's a quick flight. It's about an hour flight and um they really have 10 guys or sorry, four guys that can go in the top 10 and then another few other really good prospects as well. So, and on both sides of the ball. So, um it and we had some time. We always build in some time in our draft process for contingencies and whatnot and and we just said this would be really good to go there, see these guys, always get another touch point on them. you know, that's always good. As many touch points, I think, as you can get to understand, you know, make, you know, get comfortable with a person. Um, they have a great coaching staff there that we're able to to tap into when we're out there and talk to coach Patricia, uh, the best defensive coordinator in in college football. And, uh, he gave us great insight into his defensive guys. Coach Coach Day gave us great insight in the offensive guys. And so, it was definitely worthwhile. >> And there's so many things goes into this offseason, right? It's not just the draft stuff. It's not just the free agency. It's also coaching staff, personnel and things of that nature. For the first time, UN and DQ got to go get two new coordinators together, one offensive coordinator, one defensive coordinator, Donte Jones, David Blau, what goes into that decision- making to bring two up and cominging stars in the game here as our coordinators? >> Well, I think, you know, I think really hats off to DQ. you know, he led that process and and he did he was extremely thorough in terms of, you know, combing the league, combing every, you know, everywhere to find, you know, the different candidates of all kinds of different, you know, expertise and background and all that. I think he did a great job identifying two guys that have been so far just fantastic and and I have no doubt they they'll continue to be that once we get the guys in and and start installing everything. But in terms of where I'm at, you know, the processes that we've been through so far, free agency, they've both been awesome. And then the draft, they've both been awesome and and they're great guys to work with and just great guys to be around. So, um, that all helps and and I know they're going to be really good on the grass. And >> for the third season, UNDQ get to be in the draft room. Now, it's a new draft room this time, which I know you're excited about, but that process about collaborating, we talk about it every year, you and him being able to collaborate on these prospects. What's your favorite part about being in that draft room with DQ? >> Yeah, I think I mean one just you know sitting sitting next to them being able to to discuss things but then just you know we see same things the same way you know in terms of just football players and and what we're looking for and so you know we can kind of see all right that's a commander right there you know and you kind of you feel that and then you know draft day um that's always fun. There's a lot of dead times. You can joke around a little bit, but uh when it comes time to to get ready and make the picks, you know, we do a great job of talking through it. You know, you know, listening to everybody's opinion and but ultimately it's it's us and um you know, we we've been really good at working together. >> We're so excited again to see you and DQ there together in that draft room. AP, we can't wait. Thank you for taking the time. You know, the kids are saying, "Let AP cook." And that's exactly what we want to see. AP cook. AP, we appreciate you so much, sir. >> Appreciate it, man. >> Yes, sir. hike you with.
